home.about.title: Independent, small, biting.
home.about.p1: Archonbite is an independent game studio. With QuizNight our focus is games that bring people to the same table: the TV is the stage, the phone is the controller, the server is the game master.
home.about.p2: This site has no cookies and no trackers; everything, fonts included, is loaded from the site itself.
home.about.v1.d: QuizNight runs in the browser: no download, no store, no Bluetooth pairing.
home.about.v2.d: Players do not need an account; open the phone page and you are in the room.
home.about.v3.d: The interface is in Turkish and English; the questions are Turkish for now.
home.about.v4.d: Only the server keeps time, answers and score; the phone just says what you want to do.

play.steps.title: Start in three steps
play.s1.p: Open the game in your TV or computer browser and press Start Game. A big QR code and a 6-character room code appear.
play.s2.p: Scan the QR with your phone camera, type a nickname and pick a character. You can also type the code by hand.
play.s3.p: The leader presses Start. Questions on the TV, answers on your phone; risk and sabotage choices are on the phone too.
play.need.title: What you need
play.need.1: One screen: a TV with a browser, a computer or a laptop plugged into a projector.
play.need.3: Internet. Phones do not need to be on the same Wi-Fi as the TV.
play.need.4: No account needed; nothing to download.
play.need.note: QuizNight has so far only been tried in Chromium-based browsers (Chrome, Edge). Device tests for Safari, Firefox and TV browsers are ongoing; the smoothest experience is current Chrome or Edge.
play.venues.title: For your board-game café or game bar
play.venues.p1: In venue mode a staff member opens a timed table on the TV from their phone. The full game runs until time is up; then the current question is never cut off, results are shown and no new game can start.
play.venues.p2: You take payment at your till: the system never takes money or asks for card details. You can optionally give the winner a small reward and upload questions of your own. Our first venue partner is Gusto Board Game Cafe (Çanakkale).
guide.title: QuizNight how-to-play guide | Archonbite
guide.desc: How to play QuizNight: setup, joining a room, round types, risk and sabotage rules, power limits, tips, accessibility, venue mode and FAQ.
guide.lead: The TV is the stage, the phone is the controller, the server is the game master. The times and points in this guide come from the game's real settings; numbers may change as the game is updated.
guide.s1.p1: QuizNight is played by 2 to 8 people. You need a screen with a browser (TV, computer, projector) and everyone's own phone.
guide.s1.l1: On the TV: open the game's address and press Start Game. A big QR code and a room code appear.
guide.s1.l2: On the phones: scan the QR with the camera, or type the room code into the box on the Play page.
guide.s1.l3: Nickname and character: a nickname of 2 to 16 characters; pick a character from the list and tap Join.
guide.s1.l4: The leader (the first player, with a crown next to their name) starts the game; at least 2 players are needed.
guide.s1.note: The same Wi-Fi is not required: the TV can be at home and a player on mobile data. All communication goes through the server over the internet.
guide.s1.img1: The lobby on the TV: QR code, room code and players
guide.s1.img2: The join screen on a phone
guide.s2.h: Joining a room and the lobby
guide.s2.p1: In the lobby the leader sets these from their phone:
guide.s2.l2: Difficulty: Easy, Medium or Hard; the game's difficulty director adjusts questions around your choice.
guide.s2.l3: Categories: all mixed, or the ones you pick.
guide.s2.l4: Reduce disturbing effects: every player can switch it on in their own phone; a mild time cut replaces Fog and Shuffle.
guide.s2.p2: If your phone sleeps or the connection drops, open the game again in the same browser; you return to your seat. If the leader drops, the leader role can pass to someone else.
guide.s3.p1: Every question goes through the stages below. The server keeps the clocks; the phone only says what you want to do.
guide.s3.r1d: Pick your stake (Safe, Risk, High), optionally use Double Down or another risk, and press Ready.
guide.s3.r1t: 12 s (16 s in Risk and Final rounds)
guide.s3.r2d: Players with a token may hit a rival; nobody sees who did it. Without a token you get a calm waiting screen.
guide.s3.r3d: The question is read on the TV and four options appear on your phone. Options carry a colour, a letter and a shape. You earn a speed bonus for remaining time.
guide.s3.r3t: 12 to 25 s depending on the round type
guide.s3.r4d: It locks when everyone has answered or time is up. The correct answer, who picked what and a short "did you know" note are shown.
guide.s3.r5d: Points are applied, the results of powers (Shield, Duel, Pot…) are shown and the ranking updates.
guide.s3.p2: The question text is hidden on the phone by default, because the TV is the stage. The "Show question" button reveals it on the phone too.
guide.s4.p1: A game mixes several round types. Base points are for a correct answer; the speed bonus scales with the time left and is not multiplied by the stake.
guide.s4.std.d: The default round. Safe, Risk or High stake.
guide.s4.spd.d: Short time, big speed bonus. Be late and the chance is gone.
guide.s4.rsk.d: A symmetric stake ladder: when wrong, you lose the stake (200 and 300).
guide.s4.crd.d: The reveal shows how everyone answered: "everybody said A" moments.
guide.s4.fin.d: Higher base points. On the very last question there is no safe option: a stake is mandatory.
guide.s4.p2: The final stage: the last questions of the game (a third of the total; at least 1, at most 5) are the final and pay 200 base points. The mandatory stake applies only to the very last question, so the final is not a coin flip.
guide.s5.p1: In Risk time you pick your stake: if right, your base points are multiplied by it; if wrong, you lose the stake. Your score never drops below zero.
guide.s5.p2: In the table the first number is the multiplier and the second is the points you lose when wrong. Example: Risk in a Classic round pays base 100 × 2 = 200 plus the speed bonus when right and costs 100 when wrong.
guide.s5.p3: One big gamble per question: High, All in, Double Down and a Duel are the "big gambles"; you may use only one of them per question. Pot, Cover and 50/50 are small and combine with any of them.
guide.s5.p4: No combination of stake and powers can lift a gain above 3 times base plus speed (5 times in the final).
guide.s6.p1: Power counts are per game; using one spends it, even if you turn out wrong.
guide.s6.dd.d: 2 per game. If right, your gain is ×2; if wrong, 200 extra points are lost on top of the stake. It cannot be combined with High or All in.
guide.s6.ff.d: 1 per game. Two wrong options are removed; in return the gain for that question is halved.
guide.s6.sh.d: 1 per game. It automatically blocks the first sabotage aimed at you; the TV says "Shield blocked it".
guide.s6.cv.d: 1 per game. You pay half of the stake's loss now; if you are wrong or do not answer you lose nothing more. It cannot be combined with Double Down.
guide.s6.du.d: 2 per game. Challenge a rival; if they accept, 80 points move when exactly one of you is right, and the faster takes 40 if both are right. It only happens when both want it; it cannot be combined with High, All in or Double Down.
guide.s6.po.d: 2 per game. Everyone who joins puts in 30 points; those who are right share the pot and the remainder goes to the fastest. At least 3 players are needed; if nobody is right, the antes are returned.
guide.s7.p1: Sabotage disturbs a rival's decision or presentation; it never falsifies the result of an answer or the score. Everyone starts the game with one sabotage token and earns more with correct-answer streaks (at 3, 6 and 9); you can hold at most 2.
guide.s7.jam.d: The target's answer time shrinks by 2 seconds (never more than 15% of the window).
guide.s7.shf.d: The target's options swap places once.
guide.s7.fog.d: One option is hidden for 1.5 seconds.
guide.s7.lck.d: The target cannot use one joker on the next round.
guide.s7.tax.d: 25% is taken from the target's next gain (it lapses if no gain comes within 3 rounds).
guide.s7.cap.d: The target's highest stake in the next question is Risk. Not usable in the final.
guide.s7.cut.d: 20% of the target's next gain (at most 30 points) goes to you. It is not aimed at the leader or at a player with no points.
guide.s7.blk.d: The target's phone hides its countdown for one question; the TV's clock stays visible.
guide.s7.p2: Limits: sabotage opens in round 3 at the earliest and is closed in the final stage. An attacker rests for 2 rounds; at most 2 sabotages happen per round; a player is targeted at most 3 times per game, with a gap of 2 rounds between hits. Nobody is ever unable to play a whole round.
guide.s7.img1: Choosing a sabotage on the phone
guide.s8.l1: Open it full screen in the TV browser; for sound you may be asked to press OK with the remote on first launch.
guide.s8.l2: Aim the TV at players' eye level so the QR code can be scanned from a distance; if there is glare, try the High Contrast theme.
guide.s8.l3: Pick Medium or Hard for a big group, and a 5-question game for a short evening.
guide.s8.l4: Instead of explaining the rules, play a 5-question trial game; the Risk and Sabotage screens explain themselves.
guide.s8.l5: The server keeps time, answers and score; nothing can be faked from a phone.
guide.s8.l6: If your TV has no browser, connect a laptop with HDMI or cast your screen.
guide.s9.l1: Answer options are never separated by colour alone: each has a letter and a shape (triangle, diamond, circle, square).
guide.s9.l2: A High Contrast theme (pure black background, white text) can be chosen in settings; colour palettes are chosen to suit colour-blind players.
guide.s9.l3: "Reduce disturbing effects" on the phone and the device's reduced-motion setting are supported.
guide.s9.l4: Text on the TV stays inside the central 90% of the screen, in large type.
guide.s9.l5: Timed screens show the time both as a number and as a ring.
guide.s9.note: Tests for glare, overscan on real TVs and with colour-blind players have not been done yet; feedback is welcome.
guide.s10.p1: A timed table for board-game cafés: the customer pays the entry fee at the till and asks for QuizNight; staff open a table on the TV from the venue panel on their phone (for example 60 minutes).
guide.s10.l1: Until time is up the full game is open and runs by itself. The TV shows the remaining time next to the room code (yellow in the last 5 minutes, red in the last minute).
guide.s10.l2: When time runs out the current question is not cut off; it finishes, results are shown and no new game starts. Staff can add +15, +30 or +60 minutes and the table carries on where it was.
guide.s10.l3: The app never takes money or asks for card details; it only keeps time.
guide.s10.l4: An optional winner reward (for example "A drink on us"): a single-use code appears on the winner's phone and is checked at the till in the panel. A tie wins nothing.
guide.s10.l5: The venue owner can upload their own questions (board games, the neighbourhood, house jokes) as CSV; they appear only on that venue's tables.
guide.s10.cta: Write to us about venue mode
guide.q1: Do I need to create an account?
guide.a1: Players do not need an account: scan the QR and type a nickname.
guide.q2: Must the phones be on the same Wi-Fi as the TV?
guide.a2: No. Everyone connects to the server over the internet; mobile data works too.
guide.a3: At least 2 and at most 8 players.
guide.q4: What language are the questions in?
guide.a4: The interface is in Turkish and English. The questions are Turkish for now; there is no question bank in other languages yet.
guide.a5: Pricing has not been decided yet. It will be announced on this page and in the news when it is.
guide.q6: My phone went to sleep, what do I do?
guide.a6: Open the game's address again in the same browser; you come back where you left off.
guide.q7: What if a question is wrong?
guide.a7: On the reveal screen you can report the question; a few serious reports take it out of the game.
guide.a8: See the privacy page for details: Privacy and cookies.
guide.a9: So far only Chromium-based browsers (Chrome, Edge) have been tried. Tests for other browsers and TVs are ongoing.
legal.title: Privacy and cookies | Archonbite
legal.desc: The Archonbite site uses no cookies and has no trackers. Privacy, contact and draft legal text.
legal.notice: This page is a draft and is not legal advice. It must be reviewed by a lawyer before launch (KVKK and GDPR).
legal.s1.p: This website sets no cookies, has no trackers or ad networks and makes no requests to third-party servers (everything, fonts included, comes from this site). Your language choice is kept only in your own browser's local storage (localStorage) and is not sent to us.
legal.s2.p: Our hosting provider may keep standard access logs (IP address, time, requested page) for security and operation, as every site does. This site has no user accounts, forms or comments.
legal.s3.p: If a game page has a trailer and you press Play, the video provider's server is loaded and the provider's own privacy rules apply. Until you press it, no request is made.
legal.s4.p: The game's own privacy, terms and support pages live inside the game and on the game server; this site does not replace them.
